title: Entropic independence via sparse localization
summary: Entropic independence is a structural property of measures that underlies modern proofs of functional inequalities, notably (modified) log-Sobolev inequalities, via ``annealing'' or local-to-global schemes. Existing sufficient criteria for entropic independence typically require spectral independence and/or uniform bounds on marginals under \emph{all} pinnings, which can fail in natural canonical-ensemble models even when strong mixing properties are expected.
